Súpis Židov (census of Jews ordered February 1942 before the deportations): 619 persons listed in Trebišov (total town population 1940: 7650)
Deportations began in spring 1942, mainly to Auschwitz-Birkenau and Majdanek; no deportation count given

From 4 May 1942 Hlinka Guard units from Nováky organized transports in eastern Slovakia; their first concentration action in Trebišov met with protests from the local non-Jewish population; no count given
Jews of Trebišov deported in May 1942 (2 and 5 May) to Lublin (Majdanek) together with the Jews of Sečovce; no count given

About 300 Jews from Sečovce and about 250 from adjoining villages were brought to the abandoned barracks in Trebišov before the 5 May 1942 transport to the Lublin area; transit count of non-residents - not Trebišov's population

Post-war Jewish religious community (ŽNO) wrote on 10 Nov 1949 that its members had emigrated and the few remaining would leave by end of November; the community was being liquidated. Not recorded as 0 since a few still remained

In 1951 the Rabbi of Trebišov gave a Torah scroll to departing Nicholas Fenyö as 'the population was gone'; indicates a residual presence (a rabbi) only. The page's figure of 60 Jews in 1950 refers to Sečovce - not used
